title: Medical Microinstruments Raises $125M In Series D To Scale Robotic Microsurgery
source_used: Medical Device Network and Startupbusiness.it (Medtech Insight page is behind a login)
key_facts: MMI (Medical Microinstruments) raised $125 million in a Series D funding round, announced on 8 Oct 2026.
The round was oversubscribed and led by existing investor BioStar Capital, with Angelini Ventures, S3 Ventures and an unnamed strategic investor.
The money is for wider sales of the Symani Surgical System in the US and other key markets and for clinical trials.
Symani is a robotic system that helps surgeons make very small, precise movements in microsurgery and reduces tiredness in long operations.
About 50 Symani systems are installed and about 3,500 complex microsurgical procedures have been done worldwide (Startupbusiness, from MMI's statement).
Part of the money funds the REMIND study (NCT07178210), which tests whether Symani can safely do microsurgery on neck lymph nodes in patients with Alzheimer's disease.
The Alzheimer's idea rests on some researchers' proposal that such surgery might help clear harmful proteins from the brain; REMIND's main aim is only safety.
Mark Toland, chief executive of MMI, said the company now wants to turn adoption into large-scale deployment.
quote_evidence: Florida-based robotics specialist, MMI, has banked $125m in a Series D funding round, financially fortifying the company as it looks to expand market access and generate further data on its robotic microsurgery system.
The REMIND study’s primary goal, however, is to determine if Symani is safe for use in this procedure and patient population.

“We have demonstrated that there is a demand for robotic microsurgery at world-leading institutions. Now, our aim is to translate this adoption into large-scale deployment,” says Mark Toland, CEO of MMI, in a statement.
why_it_matters_hint: Fresh money lets a surgical-robot maker put its microsurgery system in more hospitals and test it in new uses.
